answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a bonded-entry registry: every new agent locks collateral through a single gated inlet, and that deposit serves as an anchor tying the identity to one ledger key. Duplicates cannot reuse a bond, so an attacker wanting a thousand fake voices must fund a thousand separate deposits. A periodic juniper audit slashes any deposit whose identity fails a liveness check. The attacker's cost therefore rises linearly with every forged agent, while an honest agent pays once and reclaims its stake on exit.
